summary: Establishes an income tax deduction for cash and credit card tips received which are considered wages or compensation.

title: Industry Partnership Fund Tax Credit
summary: AN ACT TO AMEND THE SOUTH CAROLINA CODE OF LAWS BY AMENDING SECTION 12-6-3585, RELATING TO THE INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIP FUND TAX CREDIT, SO AS TO PROVIDE FOR AN INCREASE IN THE AGGREGATE CREDIT FROM NINE MILLION TO TWELVE MILLION DOLLARS FOR TAX YEARS AFTER 2022. - RATIFIED TITLE

title: AN ACT TO AMEND TITLE 30 OF THE DELAWARE CODE RELATING TO EXCLUSION OF MILITARY PENSIONS FROM TAXABLE INCOME.
summary: This Act defines “United States military pension” for the exclusion for taxable income.

title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
summary: Increases the motion picture, digital media, and film production income tax credit for qualified productions that utilize qualified production facilities located within the State.  Changes the cap amount and aggregate cap amount of the motion picture, digital media, and film production income tax credit to unspecified amounts.  Imposes the manufacturing GET rate on motion picture, digital media, and film productions and repeals the provision in the definition of "qualified production costs" that applied the term to mean costs incurred that are subject to the highest GET rate.  Exempts from the

title: SNAP; mandatory employment and training..
summary: Requires Arizona to mandate that able-bodied adults under age 60 receiving SNAP benefits participate in a federal employment and training program, with enumerated exemptions for caregivers, students, employed individuals, and others.

title: Income tax; extend repealer for new cut and sew jobs in upholstered furniture industry and bring forward certain statutes.
summary: Extends the repeal date to January 1, 2029 for the Mississippi income tax credit of $2,000 per year for five years for each full-time employee in a new cut-and-sew job at an upholstered household furniture manufacturing facility, and brings forward alcoholic beverage licensing sections for possible amendment.

title: Various tax matters.
summary: Amends and adds state income tax statutes to conform with certain provisions enacted in Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1) (commonly known as One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025). Specifies rounding provisions for cash transactions with regard to the penny phaseout. Amends state income tax withholding provisions for gambling winnings. Amends the definition of "contribution" for purpose of the state income tax credit for contributions to an ABLE account. Amends provisions regarding computation of specified research or experimental expenditures. Authorizes the department of state revenue (department) to

title: Revise income taxes related to retired military members
summary: Expands Montana's income tax exemption for military pension, retirement, and survivor benefits by broadening eligibility to residents who became or remained Montana residents after a specified date, removing the prior 5-year cap on claiming the exemption, and repealing the exemption's statutory sunset.

title: Income tax; extend repealer on tax credit for certain charges for using certain port and airport facilities.
summary: Extends the sunset date to December 31, 2029 for Mississippi income tax credits available to taxpayers using state port facilities for cargo export and airport facilities for cargo import/export, and requires the Mississippi Development Authority to continue annual reporting to the legislature on the credits' economic impact.

title: Concerning school library information and technology programs.
summary: Requires every Washington school district board to adopt a policy ensuring all students have access to school library information and technology programs, mandates procedures for student access, and strengthens the statutory definition and staffing standards for these programs including qualified teacher-librarians.

title: Enslaved Ancestors College Access Scholarship and Memorial Program; scholarships, administration.
summary: Enslaved Ancestors College Access Scholarship and Memorial Program; parameters. Prohibits any such institution from passing the cost of any scholarship program established in accordance with the provisions of the Enslaved Ancestors College Access Scholarship and Memorial Program to other enrolled students by increasing the rate of tuition or mandatory fees. The bill also requires the State Council of Higher Education for Virginia to (i) establish a work group that consists of a representative of each institution that participates in the Program that meets at least semiannually to discuss Progr

title: Relates to recovery for certain overpayments
summary: Prohibits the higher education services corporation from seeking recovery of awards made in error during certain academic years due to administrative error.

title: Early Childhood Local System Consolidation
summary: Current law establishes a statewide integrated system of early childhood councils (councils) to improve and sustain the availability, accessibility, capacity, and quality of early childhood services. The act expands the powers, functions, and responsibilities of a council in implementing a comprehensive system of early childhood and family support programs and services (programs and services) within the council's community.     Current law establishes local coordinating organizations (LCOs) to increase access to, coordinate, and allocate funding for programs and services through work with the

title: SCH CD-PHONICS EDUCATION
summary: Amends the School Code. Provides that school districts shall teach students how to read using phonics.

title: Child Care Provider Licensing & Quality
summary: The bill requires the executive director of the department of early childhood (department) to make reasonable efforts to expand and standardize the use of a digital data platform as a centralized digital file system for certain child care provider information (digital provider file system). The digital provider file system must integrate adopt rules concerning the requirements for licensed child care facilities to maintain up-to-date employee records in the professional development information system currently administered by the department. and must house records related to staff background c

title: "Georgia Promise Scholarship Act"; public schools with a state-wide attendance zone and certain charter schools shall not be included in the separate list of public schools annually reported by the Office of Student Achievement; provide
summary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Code Section 20-14-27 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to required reports and publication format relative to education accountability assessment programs, so as to provide that public schools with a state-wide attendance zone and certain charter schools shall not be included in the separate list of public schools annually reported by the Office of Student Achievement for purposes of the "Georgia Promise Scholarship Act"; to provide for an effective date; to repeal conflicting laws; and for other purposes.

title: Education: public school academies; certain authorizer and educational management organization information on school signage, advertising, and promotional materials; require. Amends sec. 523 of 1976 PA 451 (MCL 380.523).
summary: Amends Michigan's public school academy law governing urban high school academies by updating contract requirements, prioritizing applicants with financial commitments and net assets of at least $50 million, and setting detailed governance, accountability, and transparency standards for urban charter high school operators.

title: Education, Dept. of - As enacted, allows a local board of education or public charter school governing body that has not received funding from the department for purposes of awarding its teachers the bonus authorized in the Education Freedom Act of 2025 to pass the required resolution and notify the department of the same within 21 calendar days from the date the Act becomes a law, to receive funding from the department to award bonuses to teachers employed in the 2024-2025 school year.  - Amends Chapter 7 of the Public Acts of the First Extraordinary Session of 2025.
summary: Amends Tennessee's Education Freedom Act of 2025 to extend one-time teacher bonus eligibility (minimum $2,000) to districts and public charter schools that had not yet received funding under that school choice act, conditioned on adopting the required resolution by June 1, 2026.

title: AN ACT RELATING TO EDUCATION -- REGIONAL VOCATIONAL SCHOOLS--ESTABLISHMENT OF CHARTER PUBLIC SCHOOLS
summary: Requires all certified independent or district charter schools upon application for a renewal of said charter or an application for a new charter school to provide a union neutrality clause in the charter.

title: students; interscholastic activities; eligibility; costs
summary: Allows private school students who reside within a public school's attendance area to try out for and participate in interscholastic activities at that public school on equal terms with enrolled students, and caps participation fees at the student's pro rata share of program costs.

title: Charter schools; renaming the Charter Schools Incentive Fund; directing transfer of certain remaining balance; modifying certain calculation. Effective date. Emergency.
summary: Amends Oklahoma's charter school funding statutes to rename the Charter Schools Incentive Fund (adding closure reimbursement as a purpose), expand allowable uses to include charter school closure costs, and adjust the revolving fund structure for state aid payments to charter and virtual charter schools.

title: Private elementary or secondary school; use of public funds for tuition, standards.
summary: Use of public funds for private elementary or secondary  school tuition; standards. Establishes several requirements and conditions  relating to the use of certain public funds enumerated in the bill to fund student  tuition at private elementary and secondary schools in the Commonwealth,  including (i) requiring all students enrolled at  schools who receive such funds to take Standards of Learning assessments; (ii) requiring all such schools to receive accountability  ratings from the Board of Education; and (iii)  prohibiting such schools from discriminating in admissions, enrollment,  disci

title: ASSESSORS: Authorizes limited increases in annual compensation for assessors in each parish (EG +$847,031 LF EX See Note)
summary: Amends a Louisiana bill to add an exception barring any assessor who, for taxable years after December 31, 2023, assessed property in violation of the homestead exemption (R.S. 47:6001) from receiving an otherwise-authorized compensation increase.

title: Extends the authority for the town of Brookhaven to impose a real estate transfer tax with revenues therefrom to be deposited into a community preservation fund
summary: Extends the authority for the town of Brookhaven to impose a real estate transfer tax with revenues therefrom to be deposited into a community preservation fund until 2045.

title: Relates to community preservation funds for the town of Orangetown
summary: Authorizes the town of Orangetown to establish community preservation funds; establishes a real estate transfer tax with revenues therefrom to be deposited in said community preservation fund; provides for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof.

title: LOC GOV-RESIDENTIAL ENERGY
summary: Amends the Counties Code and the Illinois Municipal Code. Provides that a county or a municipality may not adopt or enforce an ordinance, rule, or other measure that would regulate the installation or inspection of a residential energy backup system, including on a building with a shared roof. Defines "residential energy backup system". Effective June 1, 2026.

title: Promoting the integration of fusion technology within state clean energy policies.
summary: Integrates fusion energy into Washington's clean energy policy framework by directing state agencies to identify permitting and siting pathways for fusion facilities, and by including fusion energy projects as eligible for clean energy project of statewide significance designation.

title: Provides that fusion energy and fusion technology companies are eligible to receive benefits under certain economic incentive programs.
summary: Directs the New Jersey Economic Development Authority to adopt rules making fusion energy and fusion technology companies eligible for the same economic incentive programs as renewable energy and emerging technology companies, while explicitly excluding fusion from the NJ Clean Energy Program.

title: RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HAWAIIAN HOME LANDS.
summary: Establishes a permitted interaction group within the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands.  Appropriates funds to the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands to continue geophysical data collection, investigation, exploration, and identification of geothermal resources on Hawaiian home lands.  Authorizes DHHL to hire consultants.  Effective 7/31/2050.  (SD1)

title: RENEWABLE ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE STUDY GROUP
summary: Requests that New Mexico's Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department create a study group to develop recommendations for accelerating permitting and deployment of community- and utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure, with findings due by November 1, 2026.

title: Climate change.
summary:
Existing law establishes the State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission (Energy Commission) under the direction of a chairperson. Existing law provides an annual salary for members and for the chairperson and prescribes a method by which those salaries may be increased.

Existing law grants an additional salary increase of 5% in each of the 2023–24, 2024–25, and 2025–26 fiscal years for members of the Energy Commission.
